claims.claim: Making a small payment on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: This supports nonrevival by payment alone once the claim is barred. Before then, a qualifying payment of principal or interest on a promissory note starts a new period; the text sets no minimum amount.

claims.claim: Signing something on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: The content of the writing matters. The statute does not rule out an effective acknowledgment or promise signed by the party to be charged.

claims.claim: The applicable limit is four years.
claims.note: No provided text establishes the length of the applicable period.

claims.claim: The limit keeps running no matter what you pay.
claims.quote: to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note, and to start the running of a new period of time
claims.note: The statute expressly provides for a new period with each qualifying note payment before the claim is barred.

claims.claim: The limit keeps running no matter what you sign.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: The statute distinguishes a signed acknowledgment or promise from other writings.

claims.claim: You can safely make a payment without affecting the limitations defense.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time, but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: The assurance disregards the risk of starting a new period on a note before the existing period expires.

claims.claim: You can safely sign a payment plan without affecting the limitations defense.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: The text gives no assurance for a payment plan containing a signed acknowledgment or promise.

flags.text: The draft denies the statutory effect of a qualifying payment before a note claim is barred.
The four-year period lacks a source.
The draft treats debts near and past the limit alike, extends the note-payment provision to debts generally, and treats all signed writings alike.
“You can safely” gives the reader personal reassurance about paying or signing.
Acting on that reassurance could weaken a limitations defense through a qualifying payment before the bar or a signed acknowledgment or promise.

result.summary: CCP-360 distinguishes starting a new period by a qualifying note payment from reviving an already barred claim by payment alone. It also makes the content of a signed writing relevant. It does not establish a four-year period or support the draft’s safety assurances.
